job.style: a diary entry or letter by a student

response.passage: Dear Diary, today our history teacher, Mr. Sharma, took us to the National Museum to see the Harappan collection. I was fascinated by the seals. He explained that the Harappans were master traders, and their extensive maritime trade with Mesopotamia led to the development of standardized weights and measures. It is incredible to think that this happened around 2500 BCE. My friend Arjun was more interested in the drainage systems, while Priya kept staring at the terracotta figurines. We saw 12 distinct types of seals in one display case. Mr. Sharma mentioned that the decline of the civilization is still a mystery, but some scholars believe that shifting river courses caused the cities to be abandoned. I felt tired after walking for 3 hours, but seeing the actual artifacts made the textbook chapters come alive. It is not just about old bricks; it is about how people lived thousands of years ago. I wonder if they ever felt as curious as I do today. Tomorrow, we have to write a report on the trade routes, so I better start researching tonight.
response.summary: A student visits a museum to learn about the Harappan civilization. They observe artifacts like seals and drainage systems while reflecting on the civilization's trade and eventual decline.
